FN-HGPS933-1
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 609
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Rex Reynolds
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 03/17/2026
House Bill 609 as introduced would expand the source of monies that may be deposited into the
Neighbors Helping Neighbors Fund to include grants, gifts, contributions, other revenue sources
directed by the Legislature, and any other lawful sources.
This bill could also increase expenditures from the fund by an undetermined amount dependent
any weatherization assistance provided by the Alabama Department of Economic and
Community Affairs (ADECA) to individuals that would not otherwise qualify for such
assistance under current law by increasing the threshold for eligibility for the program from
households having an income level at or below 125% of the poverty level, under current law, to
households having an income level at or below 200% of the poverty level.
Additionally, this bill would authorize ADECA to contract with certain nonprofit corporations
to provide energy assistance instead of requiring that these funds be provided to designated
community action agencies or county governments to administer the program.
The current balance in the Neighbors Helping Neighbors Fund is approximately $200,000.

FN-HGPS933-2
FISCAL NOTE
House Bill 609
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Representative Rex Reynolds
Analyst: Jennifer Farish Date: 03/18/2026
House Bill 609 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund would expand
the source of monies that may be deposited into the Neighbors Helping Neighbors Fund to
include grants, gifts, contributions, other revenue sources directed by the Legislature, and any
other lawful sources and would remove contributions from taxpayers received by the
Department of Revenue as a source of funding for the fund.
This bill could also increase expenditures from the fund by an undetermined amount dependent
any weatherization assistance provided by the Alabama Department of Economic and
Community Affairs (ADECA) to individuals that would not otherwise qualify for such
assistance under current law by increasing the threshold for eligibility for the program from
households having an income level at or below 125% of the poverty level, under current law, to
households having an income level at or below 200% of the poverty level.
Additionally, this bill would authorize ADECA to contract with certain nonprofit corporations
to provide energy assistance instead of requiring that these funds be provided to designated
community action agencies or county governments to administer the program.
The current balance in the Neighbors Helping Neighbors Fund is approximately $200,000.
